title: Build business judgement by watching, reading and explaining one business idea a day
description: Consultants connect numbers to business decisions. You want to recognise familiar patterns, not copy an executive’s personality or body language.
hook: If you do not come from a business background, case language can feel foreign at first. A few minutes a day of the right kind of reading and watching changes that quickly.
body:
Why this matters

Consultants connect numbers to business decisions. You want to recognise familiar patterns, not copy an executive’s personality or body language.

Three exercises (15 to 20 minutes a day)

Watch a business discussion

Try Shark Tank or a founder/CEO interview. Pause to ask: What is the business model? How does it make money? What would I recommend? Watch how the speaker uses a measured tone, posture, pauses and simple words. Practise these techniques, but keep your own natural style.

Learn one useful business idea

For example: unit economics, customer acquisition cost, churn, pricing power, contribution margin, switching costs or operating leverage.

Explain it in your own words

Give a 60-second explanation using a real or fictional company. Record one useful phrase in your vocabulary notes.

Keep it small

Short and regular beats long and occasional. Ten minutes most days will do more than two hours on a Sunday. Tick it off and move on with your day.
outro: Read it once, then try it on a practice case today while it is fresh. One real attempt teaches more than three re-reads. All three routines, with links to free tools, are on the interview skills page.
